record.original_question: For the antiferromagnetic spin-1/2 Heisenberg XXX spin chain, consider ground-state correlation functions of local spin operators on sequential lattice sites, including quantities such as the emptiness formation probability. These correlation functions are known to be expressible as polynomials in ln 2 and in values of the Riemann zeta function, or equivalently the alternating zeta series, at odd arguments with rational coefficients. Find an efficient and tractable description of the rational coefficients that appear in these polynomial expressions.

evidence.quote: Conjecture. 1 (Boos, Korepin 2001) Any correlation function of the XXX spin chain can be represented as a polynomial in ln 2 and values of Riemann zeta function at odd arguments with rational coefficients [13],[14].

However we still not have explicit expressions for the rational coefficients that enter in the expression for the correlation functions as polynomials in ln 2 and Riemann zeta function at odd arguments. Such a description will provide a tractable formula for the correlations of the XXX spin chain.

Open problem: Efficient description of the rational coefficients which appear in the expression for the correlation functions of the XXX spin chain as a polynomial in alternating zeta series at odd arguments.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the antiferromagnetic spin-1/2 Heisenberg XXX chain on the infinite one-dimensional lattice, with Hamiltonian
H = J ∑_{k∈ℤ} ( S^x_k S^x_{k+1} + S^y_k S^y_{k+1} + S^z_k S^z_{k+1} ),  J > 0,
where S^α_k = (1/2)σ^α_k act on the k-th copy of ℂ^2. Let |GS⟩ denote the (unique, in the thermodynamic limit) ground state at zero temperature and zero external magnetic field, and let ⟨·⟩ denote the ground-state expectation value.

For any positive integer n, consider the ground-state correlation functions of products of local spin operators acting on n consecutive sites, e.g. ⟨S^{α_1}_1 S^{α_2}_2 ⋯ S^{α_n}_n⟩, and in particular the emptiness formation probability
P(n) = ⟨ ∏_{k=1}^n ( 1/2 + S^z_k ) ⟩,
which is the probability that the first n consecutive sites are all in the spin-up state.

It is known (and assumed throughout) that every such n-site ground-state correlation function can be written as a polynomial, with rational coefficients, in ln 2 and in the values ζ(2m+1), m ≥ 1, of the Riemann zeta function at odd integer arguments (equivalently, in values of the alternating zeta series ζ_a(s) = ∑_{k≥1} (−1)^{k−1}/k^s at odd s).

Problem: Provide an efficient and tractable closed-form description of the rational coefficients appearing in these polynomial expressions, valid for arbitrary n and for arbitrary choices of the local spin operators on the n consecutive sites.
artifact.category_tag: Heisenberg XXX spin chain correlation functions
artifact.status_search_result: Literature searches indicate that while explicit polynomial expressions in ln 2 and odd zeta values have been computed for short-range correlators (up to about n=6 or 7 sites) using the qKZ equation, hidden Grassmann structure, and fermionic basis approaches, no efficient general closed-form description of the rational coefficients for arbitrary n-site XXX correlators is known. The problem of an efficient description of these rational coefficients remains open.

status_evidence.title: XXX Spin Chain: from Bethe Solution to Open Problems
status_evidence.snippet: Open problem: Efficient description of the rational coefficients which appear in the expression for the correlation functions of the XXX spin chain as a polynomial in alternating zeta series at odd arguments.
status_evidence.claim: The problem is explicitly listed as open.

status_evidence.title: Correlation functions by Separation of Variables: the XXX spin chain
status_evidence.snippet: Develops separation-of-variables techniques for XXX correlation functions; explicit general rational-coefficient formulas in ln 2 and odd zeta values are not provided.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work continues to develop tools for XXX correlators without supplying the requested efficient closed form.
